finding.claim: Path traversal / arbitrary file read in /dl. The user-controlled `f` query parameter is joined to /srv/files with filepath.Join, which cleans `..` segments but does not confine the result to the root. A request with `f=../../etc/passwd` resolves to /etc/passwd and the handler returns its contents.
finding.source: HTTP query parameter `f` on GET /dl, served on public ingress :8082 (all interfaces) with no authentication
finding.sink: os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(root, name)) at files.go:13, with the contents written to the response at files.go:18

trace.note: /dl is registered to download on the default mux; it is publicly reachable
http.ListenAndServe(":8082") binds all interfaces, with no auth middleware
name = r.URL.Query().Get("f") is taken with no validation
filepath.Join("/srv/files", "../../etc/passwd") cleans to /etc/passwd, so the traversal escapes root
The file contents are returned to the attacker

finding.guards_checked: No prefix check, no filepath.Rel or HasPrefix confinement, no os.Root or fs.FS sandbox, no allow-list, no authentication or authorization, no middleware. filepath.Join only cleans the path. Nothing rejects `..`. The same-file avatar handler (files.go:22) does apply filepath.Base, which makes it safe, so the guard is missing only in download. Repro: curl 'http://host:8082/dl?f=../../etc/passwd' returns the contents of /etc/passwd. A normal request such as f=report.txt returns /srv/files/report.txt.

verdict.reason: files.go:12-13 passes the unvalidated `f` query value to filepath.Join(root, name) and then os.ReadFile, and Join only cleans the path, so `../../etc/passwd` resolves to /etc/passwd. files.go:18 writes the contents to the response, and :32/:34 expose /dl on :8082 with no auth. The only guard in the file is filepath.Base in avatar (:22), which download does not use.
